item.text:
I used the supplied local prior for structured context and only pulled narrative, constitutional, and contemporaneous sources for office, constraints, events, and source-family selection. I did not use the client matrix.

**Retained Sources**

- [Deutscher Bundestag - 5. Sitzung am Mittwoch, dem 8. Dezember 2021](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/protokolle/amtlicheprotokolle/ap20005-871022) | Deutscher Bundestag | 8 Dec 2021. Precise fact: Olaf Scholz was elected with 395 of 707 votes, then sworn in and the new federal government was announced. Period fit: fixes the exact start of Scholz’s chancellorship entering 2022. Ruler attribution: direct and unambiguous. Limitations: formal office event only, not policy performance. Contrary points: later coalition conflict shows the vote did not translate into unconstrained control.  
  Family: primary, constitutional, favorable.

- [Election of the Federal Chancellor](https://www.bundestag.de/en/parliament/function/chancellor) | German Bundestag | current explainer page, accessed 2026-07-22. Precise fact: the chancellor needs an absolute parliamentary majority and can only be removed by a constructive vote of no confidence. Period fit: the basic constraint structure governing Scholz throughout 2022. Ruler attribution: institutional, not personal, but directly frames his room for maneuver. Limitations: explanatory page, not a 2022 event record. Contrary points: coalition bargaining and Bundesrat votes can constrain even when the constitutional text looks strong.  
  Family: primary, constitutional.

- [Duties of the Federal Chancellor](https://www.bundeskanzler.de/bk-en/federal-chancellery/duties-of-the-federal-chancellor) | Federal Chancellery | current explainer page, accessed 2026-07-22. Precise fact: the chancellor sets the policy guidelines, chairs cabinet work, is accountable to the Bundestag, and in coalition governments policy is normally governed by coalition agreement. Period fit: this is the practical authority model for Scholz in 2022. Ruler attribution: direct, because it describes the office he held. Limitations: generic institutional explainer, not Scholz-specific and not a dated 2022 snapshot. Contrary points: individual ministers and coalition partners still retain meaningful autonomy and veto power.  
  Family: primary, institutional, favorable.

- [Koalitionsvertrag 2021 - 2025](https://www.spd.de/koalitionsvertrag2021) | SPD | 24 Nov 2021. Precise fact: the SPD, Greens, and FDP coalition set out a shared governing program focused on climate, digitalization, social policy, and pandemic recovery. Period fit: this is the inherited governing mandate Scholz carried into 2022. Ruler attribution: direct, because it defines the coalition he led. Limitations: aspirational party document; it states goals, not outcomes. Contrary points: the Russian invasion and energy shock quickly displaced parts of the original agenda.  
  Family: primary, mandate, favorable.

- [Neujahrsansprache 2022](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/service/newsletter-und-abos/bulletin/neujahrsansprache-2022-1994476) | Federal Government | 1 Jan 2022. Precise fact: Scholz framed 2021 as still dominated by the pandemic and destructive flooding, and emphasized the smooth handover to the new government. Period fit: good for inherited conditions at the opening of 2022. Ruler attribution: direct and personal. Limitations: ceremonial address, so it emphasizes continuity and resolve. Contrary points: it underplays how quickly the year would be reshaped by the war in Ukraine and the energy shock.  
  Family: primary, favorable.

- [Policy statement by Olaf Scholz, 27 February 2022 in Berlin](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/policy-statement-by-olaf-scholz-chancellor-of-the-federal-republic-of-germany-and-member-of-the-german-bundestag-27-february-2022-in-berlin-2008378) | Federal Government | 27 Feb 2022. Precise fact: Scholz declared a “watershed/Zeitenwende,” announced the 100 billion euro Bundeswehr special fund, greater than 2 percent of GDP defense spending, sanctions, and a relief package. Period fit: the central 2022 turning-point source. Ruler attribution: direct, specific, and heavily personal. Limitations: a programmatic speech, so it is stronger on intent than implementation. Contrary points: later legislative and coalition friction slowed parts of the agenda.  
  Family: primary, favorable, high-value for Chapters 2B, 4B, 7B, 8B.

- [Grundgesetzänderung für ein „Sondervermögen Bundeswehr“](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2022/kw16-sondervermoegen-890232) | Deutscher Bundestag | 2 Jun 2022. Precise fact: the Bundestag article notes the 100 billion euro special fund, the need for a two-thirds majority, and the fact that Scholz needed opposition votes to change the Basic Law. Period fit: shows the real institutional constraint on implementing the Zeitenwende. Ruler attribution: direct but not unilateral. Limitations: legislative process coverage, not policy impact. Contrary points: the source itself shows Scholz could not simply command the change through the cabinet.  
  Family: primary, institutional, constraint-focused.

- [Bundesministerium für Wirtschaft und Klimaschutz ruft Alarmstufe des Notfallplans Gas aus](https://www.bmwk.de/Redaktion/EN/Pressemitteilungen/2022/06/20220623-federal-ministry-for-economic-affairs-and-climate-action-announces-alert-level-of-the-emergency-plan-for-gas.html) | BMWK | 23 Jun 2022. Precise fact: the ministry said gas supplies from Russia had been reduced and the energy situation was tense even though security of supply was still assured. Period fit: strong evidence for the inherited energy crisis that shaped Scholz’s 2022 agenda. Ruler attribution: indirect but relevant because it was the government’s own crisis framing. Limitations: ministry perspective, so it highlights management rather than failure. Contrary points: the report does not by itself prove that Scholz personally caused or solved the shortage.  
  Family: primary, favorable, useful for Chapters 5B and 8B.

- [Inflationsrate im Jahr 2022 bei +7,9 %](https://www.destatis.de/DE/Presse/Pressemitteilungen/2023/01/PD23_022_611.html) | Statistisches Bundesamt | 17 Jan 2023, reporting on 2022. Precise fact: Germany’s annual inflation rate averaged 7.9 percent in 2022, driven largely by energy and food price spikes linked to the war in Ukraine. Period fit: a clean macro backdrop for Scholz’s 2022 domestic constraints. Ruler attribution: indirect, but highly relevant as the economic environment his government inherited and managed. Limitations: aggregate statistic, not ruler-specific. Contrary points: the shock was primarily exogenous, so it should not be over-attributed to Scholz.  
  Family: primary, independent statistics.

- [Regierungserklärung von Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/service/newsletter-und-abos/bulletin/regierungserklaerung-von-bundeskanzler-olaf-scholz-2055408) | Federal Government | 22 Jun 2022. Precise fact: Scholz linked the special fund to a new security architecture and tied Germany’s 2022 strategy to the European Council, G7 summit, and NATO summit. Period fit: shows how the chancellor connected domestic rearmament, alliance policy, and international leadership mid-year. Ruler attribution: direct and personal. Limitations: self-reporting from the chancellor’s own office. Contrary points: the speech is stronger on strategic framing than on delivery evidence.  
  Family: primary, favorable, useful for Chapters 2B, 4B, 8B.

- [Bundestag zu Waffenlieferungen: Der abwesende Kanzler](https://www.tagesschau.de/inland/innenpolitik/scholz-waffen-ukraine-101.html) | tagesschau.de | 28 Apr 2022. Precise fact: contemporaneous analysis describes intense coalition conflict over heavy weapons for Ukraine and argues Scholz was seen as cautious and slow. Period fit: useful counterweight to the official self-framing in spring 2022. Ruler attribution: direct, because the criticism is explicitly about Scholz’s leadership style and pace. Limitations: analysis, not neutral transcript evidence. Contrary points: it reflects political and journalistic judgment, and later policy steps show he did not remain static.  
  Family: independent, local-language, critical.

**Source Families To Keep Reusing**

- Primary/favorable: Bundestag plenary records, Federal Government speeches, BMWK crisis releases, Destatis releases, SPD coalition agreement.
- Primary/constraint: Bundestag procedure explainer and the special-fund parliamentary record.
- Independent/critical/local-language: tagesschau analyses.
- Best cross-chapter mix: official constitutional/parliamentary sources for office and constraints, official government speeches for event timing, BMWK/Destatis for inherited conditions, and one or two critical German-language analyses for counterweight.

**Compact Event Map**

- December 2021 to January 2022: Scholz enters 2022 as chancellor of a three-party coalition, with pandemic aftereffects, flood recovery, and a large governing agenda already on his desk.
- February 2022: Russia invades Ukraine; Scholz halts Nord Stream 2, then announces the Zeitenwende, sanctions, a 100 billion euro Bundeswehr fund, and a broader defense reset.
- March to June 2022: coalition and parliamentary bargaining shape the special fund and weapons policy; the government begins treating energy security as a central crisis.
- June 2022: gas emergency level is activated; Scholz folds the defense reset into a broader alliance strategy tied to the EU, G7, and NATO.
- July to September 2022: the government keeps reducing Russian energy dependence while inflation stays high and domestic relief measures expand.
- Late 2022: the energy price brake and related relief packages become central instruments for social and economic stabilization.

**Chapter Source Plan**

- `1B`: no retained narrative source yet; if this chapter is reopened, prioritize defense/nuclear-capability materials and German-language security reporting, because the current local prior already flags no evidence and Germany is not a nuclear weapons state.
- `2B`: use the February 27 policy statement, the special-fund parliamentary record, the gas alert-level release, and the June 22 Bundestag statement.
- `3B`: use the tagesschau weapons-debate analysis only if a narrative attribution is needed; otherwise the local prior already gives the structural rights baseline.
- `4B`: use the Bundestag election record, chancellor election explainer, chancellery duties explainer, coalition agreement, and the critical tagesschau piece.
- `5B`: use the coalition agreement, BMWK energy-crisis release, and Destatis inflation release.
- `6B`: use the coalition agreement plus the inherited-conditions framing from Scholz’s New Year address and the inflation backdrop.
- `7B`: use the chancellery duties explainer, the policy statement, the special-fund record, and the critical tagesschau piece for accountability and rule-of-law framing.
- `8B`: use the election record, chancellor duties explainer, June 22 statement, BMWK crisis release, and the critical tagesschau piece for governance-capacity and implementation constraints.
